lessons.title: സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ) — beautiful
lessons.gloss: beautiful — a new word dropped straight into the frame the last chapter built

segments.text: Say this is easy. You built that sentence one chapter ago.
സുന്ദരം — sundaraṁ — beautiful.
ഇത് സുന്ദരമാണ്. — itŭ sundaramāṇŭ — "This is beautiful."
Read what you did there. The word ends in ം, so it welds onto ആണ് the way the last chapter's two words did, and you did it without being told.
That is what a frame is for. The chapter before this one cost you a rule; this one cost you a word, and the weld came free.

segments.instruction: the same sentence about something being easy
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the same sentence about something being easy]

segments.text: What is beautiful? (സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ).) Did you need a new rule to say this is beautiful? (No — it ends in ം, like എളുപ്പം and പ്രയാസം.)

lessons.title: ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi) — beauty
lessons.gloss: beauty — and the sentence that uses it, which says beautiful

segments.text: Say this is beautiful. Then say child — you have had that word a long time.
ഭംഗി — bhaṁgi — beauty.
ഇത് ഭംഗിയാണ്. — itŭ bhaṁgiyāṇŭ — "This is beautiful."
Read the gloss again. The word means beauty, but the sentence does not say this is beauty — it says this is beautiful, and it is the way you are most likely to hear it said.
Two different things are happening here, and only one of them is new.

utterances: സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ) becomes സുന്ദരമാണ്, the m was already there.
ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi) becomes ഭംഗിയാണ്, a യ is genuinely added.

segments.text: In സുന്ദരമാണ് nothing is added at all. The ം is the sound m, and it stays; only its writing moves, because the bare sign cannot carry a vowel. You were told that last chapter.

ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi) is the other case, and you have met the reason before. It ends in a vowel, ആണ് begins with one, and Malayalam will not let two vowels sit together — so a യ slides in between them. The joining chapter said exactly that about അരിയും.
What is new is only where it happens. ഇത് എന്റെ കുട്ടിയാണ് — this is my child — has the same യ, for the same reason.

segments.instruction: which of the two actually gained a sound, and which only changed its spelling
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which of the two actually gained a sound, and which only changed its spelling]

segments.text: What is beauty? (ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi).) Why does a യ come in before ആണ്? (Two vowels will not sit together.) Is anything added in സുന്ദരമാണ്? (No — that m was already there.)

lessons.title: ഇത് സുന്ദരമല്ല (itŭ sundaramalla) — this is not beautiful
lessons.gloss: this is not beautiful — the denial welds exactly as the is-word does, which is why you already know how to build it

segments.text: Say this is beautiful. Then say the word that denies being what you were called.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the denial welds too

segments.text: ഇത് സുന്ദരമല്ല. — itŭ sundaramalla — "This is not beautiful."
You already know how that was built. അല്ല is the negative of ആണ്, and it welds on the same way:

utterances: സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ) + ആണ്, സുന്ദരമാണ് — this is beautiful.
സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ) + അല്ല, സുന്ദരമല്ല — this is not beautiful.

segments.text: Same മ, same reason: the m was always there and now has a vowel after it, so it is written with the full letter.

When you first met അല്ല it was written apart — ഞാൻ അധ്യാപകൻ അല്ല, I am not a teacher. That was a choice about writing, not a different grammar. Weld them and you get ഞാൻ അധ്യാപകനല്ല, which is as ordinary as the other.

And look at what the ൻ does there. It is the same trick as the ം: a consonant written without a vowel, which goes back to its full letter — ൻ becomes ന — the moment a vowel arrives behind it. You have already seen it: ഇത് എന്റെ മകനാണ്, this is my son.
Both ends of the same line, from one new word and one you already had.

This is how the far end of most qualities will arrive for a while: not by a second word, but by denying the first one. It is what a learner can build today, and it is what a speaker often says anyway.

segments.text: How do you say this is not beautiful? (ഇത് സുന്ദരമല്ല (itŭ sundaramalla).) Does അല്ല weld on the way ആണ് does? (Yes — same മ, same reason.) What does the ൻ of അധ്യാപകൻ do when it welds? (It goes back to ന — as in മകനാണ്.)

lessons.title: (beautiful, and not) (sundaravuṁ allāthatuṁ enna ōrmma) — from cold
lessons.gloss: cold retrieval of both ends of the line, and of the difference between a letter re-spelled and a sound added

segments.text: Close the lessons before this one. Say this is beautiful, then deny it.

utterances: word: എളുപ്പം. joined to ആണ്: എളുപ്പമാണ്. what happened: the m was already there.
word: സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ). joined to ആണ്: സുന്ദരമാണ്. what happened: the m was already there.
word: കുട്ടി. joined to ആണ്: കുട്ടിയാണ്. what happened: a യ was added.
word: ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi). joined to ആണ്: ഭംഗിയാണ്. what happened: a യ was added.

segments.text: The two halves are not the same event. In the top pair nothing is added — the m was always in the word, and only its writing moves once a vowel sits behind it. In the bottom pair a യ genuinely appears, because the word ends in a vowel and two vowels will not sit together.
And what attaches matters too, not only how the word ended: the same സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ) gives സുന്ദരവും when the and ending arrives.
ഇത് സുന്ദരമാണ്. — this is beautiful. ഇത് സുന്ദരമല്ല (itŭ sundaramalla). — this is not beautiful.
The second is not a second word. അല്ല is the negative of ആണ് and welds the same way — same മ, same reason.

So one new quality gave you both ends of a line. That is how the far end of most qualities will arrive for a while — by denying the near one, which is both what you can build today and what a speaker often says anyway.

segments.instruction: which of the four joined forms actually gained a sound, and why
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which of the four joined forms actually gained a sound, and why]

segments.text: Beautiful, and beauty? (സുന്ദരം (sundaraṁ), ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi).) Which of the two gains a sound before ആണ്? (ഭംഗി (bhaṁgi) — a യ.) And how do you deny it? (ഇത് സുന്ദരമല്ല (itŭ sundaramalla).)
